incident-bot: ALERT: [EU-WEST] High 5xx ratio detected on inference-gateway (svc: inference-gateway, env: prod-eu-west). 5xx_rate > 5/min for 3m. Triggered at 2026-03-15T01:47:58Z :rotating_light:
Maya (oncall): seeing it, I'm paging the rotation. paging now -> @Jon @Lee :phone:
Maya (oncall): quick check: dashboard EU gateway p95 latency jumped to 1.4s and 502s spiking to ~12/min, sustained for ~4m.
Jon (infra): on it, I'm looking at lb->pool health, could be a backend flapping parameter after the config push. pulling logs now.
Lee (eng-sre): adding context: we just had a small rollout to the eu-west pool 12m ago (model variant swap). Could be related.
Maya (oncall): @Sophia @Aisha any customer-reported errors?
Aisha (CS): have 2 open tickets from EU customers reporting slow responses/502s in last 10m. Marking high impact if persists.
Jon (infra): quick grep from gateway logs:
```
2026-03-15T01:44:03Z WARN upstream 502 backend timeout p99=2.1s route=/v1/generate
2026-03-15T01:45:10Z ERROR connection reset by peer model-host-7
2026-03-15T01:46:22Z WARN upstream 502 backend overload queue_len=86
```
Jon (infra): model-host-7 shows repeated connection resets, kernel IO spikes. I'm ssh-ing into host.
Lee (eng-sre): for live mitigation: recommend removing model-host-7 from rotation, enable fallback route to one of our hot spares in eu-west, and raise capacity in us-east as a temporary failover if eu throughput drops.
Maya (oncall): doing drain now: `curl -X POST https://controlplane/api/pools/eu-west/remove?instance=model-host-7` -> 202 Accepted.
incident-bot: NOTE: automated canary rollback detected ~11m ago on model-variant v2.3 -> v2.2; no failures flagged then.
Jon (infra): I see disk stalls on model-host-7, fs usage 96% on /var/cache; clearing temp cache and restarting inference-worker.
Sophia (product): is the customer impact limited to specific accounts or global in region? we need to prepare comms.
Aisha (CS): both tickets are from two different customers but similar symptoms. Marking incidents page for affected accounts: acct-redwood-analytics, acct-saasflow.
Maya (oncall): after drain, 502s dropped to ~2/min, latency p95 down to 380ms. Good mitigation.
Lee (eng-sre): mitigation worked. Putting follow-up: we need to tune alerting: current 5/min threshold fires too early during rolling deploys and creates noise. Propose switching alert from raw 5xx_rate to a composite: when 5xx_rate > 5/m AND cluster_unhealthy_hosts > 0 for 2m. Also add suppression window when deploy_tag is non-empty.
Jon (infra): agree. Also add a second alert for traffic-shift: if traffic share EU drops > 20% in 3m and US increases > 20% -> fire failover-monitor alert for ops.
Maya (oncall): I'm creating a short-runbook note in the thread:
```
Runbook excerpt:
- If 5xx spike and model-host X shows IO/disk errors -> drain instance and replace.
- If 5xx persists after draining -> shift traffic to backup pool and scale up dedicated capacity.
- Notify CS + Product with affected accounts list.
- Post-mortem: consider cache eviction policy for model-hosts.
```
Lee (eng-sre): recording the proposed Prometheus alert for review:
```
- alert: EU_5xx_and_host_failure
  expr: (sum(rate(http_requests_total{region="eu-west",code=~"5.."}[1m])) > 5)
        and (sum(up{pool="eu-west",state="draining"}) > 0)
  for: 2m
  labels:
    severity: critical
  annotations:
    summary: "EU 5xx + host failure"
```
Lee (eng-sre): also proposing a synthetic health-check across regions to detect silent failovers and traffic shifts.
Sophia (product): can we get a dashboard tile for multi-region traffic share and p95 by region? Need it for SLA reviews.
Maya (oncall): opening ticket MON-1248 to add dashboard and change alerts.
Jon (infra): putting quick patch in alertmanager to silence similar alerts for the next 30m while we stabilize: `amtool silence add --match 'alertname=High5xx' --starts now --ends +30m --comment 'stabilizing after EU failover'`
incident-bot: PAGED oncall rotation to Jon at 2026-03-15T01:49:05Z via pagerduty-bot.
Jon (infra): handoff note for night shift: if pattern recurs, escalate to infra-leads and consider cross-region traffic shift (see runbook step).
Aisha (CS): sending short message to affected customers: "We're actively mitigating increased errors in EU, we've routed traffic to backup capacity; we'll follow up with timeline once repaired." 
Maya (oncall): postmortem checklist items:
- Add disk pressure monitoring per model-host (now only aggregate)
- Adjust 5xx alert to composite rule (Lee)
- Add multi-region traffic-share dashboard + failover alert (Sophia)
- Add deploy suppression for noisier alerts (Maya)
- Runbook update and oncall training (Jon)
Lee (eng-sre): I'm creating infra change: MON-1248 -> will include alert rules, Grafana dashboard panels, and synthetic monitor. Assign to Jon and Maya.
Jon (infra): note on thresholds: empirically the eu-west baseline 5xx is ~0.5/min. We should set firing to 5x baseline or absolute >8/min depending on instance count. I'll prototype two variants and we can pick.
Maya (oncall): final state at 01:58Z: eu-west gateway health nominal, 502s ~1/min, p95 360ms. Marking incident as mitigated.
incident-bot: INCIDENT MITIGATED: [EU-WEST] High 5xx ratio resolved at 2026-03-15T01:58:19Z.
Sophia (product): thanks team. We'll prioritise multi-region dashboard for end-to-end visibility; this one would've been easier to triage with traffic-share panel.
Aisha (CS): customers updated. Keeping on watch for 2h.
Maya (oncall): logging follow-ups in MON-1248 and setting a quick post-incident sync tomorrow 10:00 UTC.
Lee (eng-sre): follow-up action: add an alert for sudden traffic shift and an automated playbook to route to regional hot-spare when EU capacity < 70% for 5m.
Jon (infra): will also add per-host disk pressure alert `node_filesystem_free_bytes` threshold; avoid whole-cluster triggers.
Maya (oncall): handing off to night rotation: @pagerduty-bot note -> next oncall is Jon at 02:00 UTC.
pagerduty-bot: Handoff recorded: on-call -> Jon (infra) starting 2026-03-15T02:00:00Z.
Maya (oncall): thanks all, closing thread for incident. :white_check_mark:
